references.text: God gives Moses stone tablets with the law and commandments written on them, which directly refers to the Ten Commandments written on two stone tablets.
Moses receives the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets inscribed by God's finger, corresponding to the two stone tablets mentioned in Deuteronomy.
Describes the two tablets as the tablets of the testimony, written on both sides with God's handwriting, confirming that the covenant was written on stone tablets.
Moses writes the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments, on the tablets at the Lord's command.
Repeats that the Lord spoke the Ten Commandments to the entire assembly and wrote them on two stone tablets.
Moses describes how he received the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant, after being on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
God commands Moses to carve out two new stone tablets and writes the Ten Commandments on them again.
Describes that the ark of the covenant contained only the two stone tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb when the Lord made a covenant with the Israelites.
Parallel to 1 Kings 8:9, confirms that there were only the two tablets in the ark that Moses placed there at Horeb.
Mentions the ark of the covenant containing the stone tablets of the covenant, confirming the New Testament understanding of the Ten Commandments as the foundation of the covenant.
